messages:
alice: Heads-up — made a quick privnet lockdown change to tighten VPC egress for keystore. Thought it was safe but seeing a bunch of GPU nodes in eu-west-1 failing to join the warm pool. Errors show KMS decrypt DENY.
ben: ugh. can you paste the error log?
alice: here's the bootstrap log snippet: `2026-03-20T10:12:03Z ERROR keystore: decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: not authorized to use key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789:key/abcd-...`
carla: that matches a policy push we rolled earlier. sec-bot just posted a config change: `privnet/egress: deny kms:* from subnet-priv-*` — did we expect that to block node role?
alice: apparently node instances use the keystore role which needs kms:Decrypt to unwrap the ephemeral keys. I didn't realize the rule matched the warmpool subnet. my bad. :grimacing:
dmitri: cost concern — nodes failing to warm mean autoscaler spun up nodes in us-east-1 to meet load, we're seeing a cross-region burst. Billing alert fired. @oncall can we throttle scale-up?
oncall: I'm on it, throttling cross-region autoscale now. reducing max surge to 10%. also, marking incident.
ben: immediate mitigation idea: allow kms:Decrypt for role arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/keystore-node within the privnet egress policy (temporary). That should let existing bootstraps finish.
carla: agree, but please also add an audit filter so we can see any other principals affected. we need an allowlist for keystore traffic until we complete the policy refactor.
sec-bot: Audit log: policy change `privnet/egress` created by infra-api@pipeline at 2026-03-20T09:59:02Z. No canary flag. Related PR: git.redwood/infra#4821.
alice: rolling the policy back now to previous rule for kms traffic. will post patch.
ben: can you do the least-privilege fix instead of full rollback? just add `Effect: Allow` for kms:Decrypt to the node role source and only for `kms:Encrypt` key id.
alice: doing that — applying rule patch and reloading firewall ACLs.
dmitri: after we restore, let's run a sweep: confirm warmpool has 95% healthy nodes, and check that no unexpected data plane egress to external regions happened. we need a postmortem to quantify cost delta.
carla: opened OPT ticket INFRA-789 for follow-up: define explicit keystore egress policy, support canary for policy changes on privnet, and add automated policy-impact tests against warmpool bootstrap flow.
oncall: monitoring: nodes started re-registering at 10:17Z. warmpool healthy count climbing.
ben: nice — keep an eye on audit logs. who signed off on the original policy PR?
carla: PR approver was "infra-api" (merged by pipeline). adding human reviewer step now.
alice: apologies all. lesson: don't apply broad egress denies without validating bootstrapping principals. will coordinate next time. :woman-shrugging:
dmitri: also recommend a cost guardrail: if cross-region burst > $X/hour trigger throttles and notify oncall + infra leads.
carla: noted. I'll include cost guardrail proposal in INFRA-789.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0319-4, severity P2, linked tickets: INFRA-789.
ben: thanks. can we schedule a 15min sync in 30min to confirm mitigations and hand off postmortem owners?
alice: yes, pinging calendar.
carla: adding postmortem owner: carla, reviewer: dmitri, security review: ben.
sec-bot: closing thread when postmortem draft is uploaded.
